question: What will Samolet's BO-P16 bond close at on 13 November 2026, as a percentage of par?

calls.reasoning: Status quo: last trade 60.21 on 2 Nov 2026 (MOEX marketdata); October closes ranged 55.6-68.1 with frequent 5-10% daily swings on restructuring news. Base anchor is the current price (random walk for a distressed bond over 9 trading days). Downside: VTB's 30 Oct statement of a creditor-led 'complex sanation agreement' (Art. 31.1 127-FZ) focused on extending debt maturities could bind bondholders; a missed/late 13 Nov coupon or an announced maturity extension could push the price into the 40s or (low-prob) below 30. Upside: October payments made on schedule; a finalised bank plan that leaves bonds untouched could lift price back to ~70. No human prediction market found (Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi/bookmakers: none).

calls.reasoning: Status quo: BO-P16 last traded 60.21 on 2 Nov after closing 60.05 on 30 Oct. October closes ranged 55.6-68.1, and news days moved the price by 5-10 points. Treat the next 9 trading days as close to a random walk. Lean slightly downward, because distressed paper with unresolved bondholder treatment tends to drift lower, and VTB's sanation remarks put extensions or haircuts on the table. Offsetting that, all October payments were on time, the 13 Nov coupon is small (~RUB 63m), Sber expects the bank deal by year-end, and the new sanation law is unlikely to apply before 2027. A paid coupon, or a deal that leaves bonds untouched, could push the price to ~70+. A missed BO-P06 coupon (5 Nov) or BO-P16 coupon, or a bondholder haircut, would push it into the 30s-40s, and I price a 4% escape below 30. Market check: none of the runs found a market on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers, and the harness search found none either.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the facts: the 2 Nov last trade of 60.21, the October path, the payment record, VTB's sanation comments, and that resolution is the clean-price CLOSE. They differ on how realized vol is expressed: Run 2 gives ~5-6% per day, Run 3 gives 2.5-3 pts per day. At a price of ~60 these are close and both imply ~8-9 pts SD over the horizon, so this is not a real dispute. Run 2 says the sanation law takes effect in 2027 at the earliest, and Run 1 describes how the mechanism works; these do not conflict, and I accept the 2027 timing, which lowers the chance of a binding bondholder action before 13 Nov. What is left is judgment about the size of the tails and the drift. I take a median a little below the current price and a 4% low escape, between Run 1/2's 3% and Run 3's 5%, because the BO-P06 and BO-P16 coupons are two separate payment tests inside the window. I carry forward the runs' shared reference class and the realized-vol dispersion basis. I had no web access on this run and retrieved nothing new.
